tasks.short: Export contacts and activities, count outcomes, check figures with the student administration, write and assemble the report, get it approved and send it.

steps.what: Counselor adds contacts and activities not yet recorded in the guidance system: copied from files into a spreadsheet today
Counselor counts students per outcome: choices made, referrals and dropouts
Counselor checks the figures against the student administration's numbers
Counselor writes the narrative and assembles reports on students and activities as required by administration
Team leader reviews the final guidance report, figures and narrative, and approves it
Counselor e-mails the approved report to school management

tasks.design: Contacts, referrals and outcomes are recorded in the student guidance system ({OTHER}), which produces the counts per outcome from the same student records the administration uses, so figures rarely differ. The counselor owns the report: checks the figures, writes the narrative and assembles it; after the team leader approves, the system publishes it to school management.
tasks.previous_blocker: Activities were copied from files into spreadsheets and counted by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Guidance systems keep contacts and outcomes as records that reports can count.
tasks.still_hard: Counts are only right if contacts are recorded; the narrative needs the counselor's view.
tasks.human_edge: Explaining what the numbers mean for students who fall through the cracks.
tasks.altitude: The counselor writes the analysis; counting disappears.

reach.task: Report to the board on guidance
reach.learn: Whether shared counts end disputes about figures.

evidence.claim: Records systems produce counts and reports from the same records staff enter.
Reports leaving the guidance team should hold counts, not data on individual students.

assumptions: Boundary: from records to the report delivered; management decisions are outside.
Input contract: contacts and outcomes recorded by the counselors; student numbers from the student administration; report layout set by the team leader; fallback is spreadsheets.
Team leader time is outside the counselor's savings.
The narrative stays the counselor's own.
s1 keeps 10 for contacts some counselors still keep only in files; s2 counts all records in the system, so it goes.
research_questions: Do figure disputes with the administration disappear?

already_counted.description: Counselor reviews generated counts for oddities.

incremental.description: Counselor records every contact and outcome in the system.

approvals.approved_version: The guidance report with its figures and narrative exactly as reviewed and approved by the team leader in s5, published once by the guidance system to school management; any change needs a new review and approval.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a third of counselors keep contacts outside the system, so s1 keeps 40 and s2 keeps 30 (46.4); high: nearly all contacts recorded as designed (62.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Answer teachers' questions, collect vacancy and labour market information, make a monthly staff update and brief teams.

steps.what: Counselor answers teachers' and staff members' questions about helping students pursue employment
Counselor collects vacancies, internships and labour market information from websites
Counselor checks the monthly update built from the vacancy list and event calendar and adds comments for staff
Counselor checks the final monthly update: vacancies still open, dates, links and the comments
Counselor sends the checked monthly update to teachers and staff
Counselor briefs teacher teams in their meetings

tasks.design: A staff page in {DOCS} answers recurring questions on procedures, internships and programmes, and a feed from regional vacancy and internship sources fills a list there. The monthly update is built from that list and the event calendar for the counselor to check and add comments; briefings and harder questions stay with the counselor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Information was searched each time and sent by e-mail.
tasks.enabler_now: Shared staff pages and vacancy feeds are standard.
tasks.still_hard: Feeds bring noise; teachers prefer asking a person.
tasks.human_edge: Helping a teacher see what a student could become.

reach.learn: Whether one list serves both roles.

evidence.claim: Vacancy and internship sources offer feeds that can fill a shared list.
Staff using AI tools need AI literacy; this design uses none.

assumptions: Boundary: from staff questions to team briefings; student coaching is outside.
Input contract: staff page kept by the counselor; vacancy feeds chosen by the counselor; event calendar kept by the guidance team; fallback is e-mail.

Briefings and the final check and send of the update do not change. About a third of staff questions are recurring ones the staff page answers, so s1 keeps 70. The staff page is an internal page the counselor edits; an ordinary save that needs no approval.
Teachers' time is outside the counselor's savings.
research_questions: Do teachers use the staff page instead of asking?

already_counted.description: Counselor checks the built monthly update.

incremental.description: Counselor keeps the staff page current.

approvals.approved_version: The monthly update with vacancies, dates, links and comments exactly as checked by the counselor in s3b, sent once to the staff mailing list; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: teachers keep asking in person and the feeds miss many regional vacancies, so s1 keeps 90 and s2 keeps 70 (18.5); high: page and feeds as designed (28.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Join curriculum meetings, gather subject choices, count demand for the master schedule, check students' clashes and evaluate programs.

steps.what: Counselor collaborates with teachers and administrators in curriculum meetings
Students choose their subjects online in the student information system
Counselor gathers students' subject choices: from paper forms today; after the change, chases missing choices and enters the few paper forms left
Counselor counts demand per subject combination for the master schedules
Counselor checks by hand whether each student's choices clash in the timetable
Students fill in the online feedback survey on the programme
Counselor evaluates programs from student feedback forms

tasks.design: Students choose subjects online in the student information system ({OTHER}), which counts demand per combination for the timetabler and lists students whose choices clash in the draft timetable for the counselor to resolve with them. Feedback forms become an online survey with a summary view; curriculum meetings stay as they are.
tasks.previous_blocker: Choices came on paper and demand and clashes were worked out in spreadsheets.
tasks.enabler_now: Student information systems take subject choices online and check them against timetables.
tasks.still_hard: Resolving clashes means talking with students about their plans.
tasks.human_edge: Helping a student keep the subject that matters for their future when the timetable says no.

reach.learn: Whether early demand counts reduce clashes.

evidence.claim: Student information systems take subject choices online and can check them against a timetable.
AI that decides access to education is high-risk; this design uses rules only.

assumptions: Boundary: from curriculum meetings to the programme evaluation; building the timetable is outside.
Input contract: subject list and allowed combinations set by school management; draft timetable from the timetabler; choices entered by students; fallback is paper forms.
Timetabler time is outside the counselor's savings.

Meetings do not change. Students' time to choose online (s2a) and to fill in the survey (s5a) is about what the paper forms took and is outside the counselor's savings. s5 keeps 70 because judging the programme stays; the summary view removes counting the forms.
research_questions: Do fewer students change subjects after the start of the year?

incremental.description: Counselor helps students who struggle with the online choice.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many students still hand in paper forms and the draft timetable changes late, so s2 keeps 60 and s4 keeps 60 (30.9); high: online choice and clash list as designed (39.8).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Plan open days and school visits, present to prospective students, answer their questions, process enrolment forms and send confirmations.

steps.what: Counselor plans recruitment activities such as open days and school visits
Counselor presents the school at open days and visits
Counselor answers prospective students' and parents' e-mails
Counselor checks changes to the website FAQ against the admission rules and dates before they go live
Counselor publishes the checked FAQ changes on the school website
Families fill in the enrolment form online and upload the required documents: on paper today
Counselor processes enrollment forms and checks the documents
Counselor checks each complete enrolment and its confirmation and intake invitation: student, programme and intake date
Counselor releases the checked confirmations and intake invitations from the student information system to the families

tasks.design: An FAQ on the school website answers common questions from prospective students and parents, and families enrol online in the student information system ({OTHER}), which checks that required documents are uploaded; the counselor checks each enrolment and releases its confirmation and intake invitation from the system. FAQ changes are checked before they go live. Planning, presenting and admission decisions stay with staff; no AI decides admission.
tasks.previous_blocker: Enrolment was on paper and every question was answered by e-mail.
tasks.enabler_now: Student information systems offer online enrolment with document upload.
tasks.still_hard: Families without digital skills need help; admission rules need human judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Making a nervous twelve-year-old feel welcome at the open day.

reach.learn: Whether online enrolment cuts registration errors.

evidence.claim: Student information systems offer online enrolment with document upload and confirmations.
AI that determines admission to education is high-risk; this design uses only completeness checks.

assumptions: Boundary: from planning recruitment to intake invitations; admission decisions are outside.
Input contract: required documents list set by the student administration; FAQ kept by the counselor; fallback is paper forms.
Administration time is outside the counselor's savings.
Families' form time is shown in s6 as customer time, not as the counselor's savings; it is not counted again as new work.
research_questions: Do incomplete enrolments fall with online checks?

approvals.approved_version: The confirmation and intake invitation for each enrolment, with student, programme and intake date exactly as checked by the counselor in s4b, sent once by the student information system to that family; any change needs a new check.
The FAQ changes exactly as checked by the counselor in s3a against the admission rules and dates, published once on the school website; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: about half of families still enrol on paper and the FAQ covers fewer questions, so s4 keeps 70 and s3 keeps 80 (18.7); high: online enrolment and FAQ as designed (27.9).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The career counselor keeps meetings, presentations and analysis; counting, gathering and paper enrolments shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A counselor whose reports, choices and enrolments run from one set of records, leaving time for students.

job.title: Educational, Guidance, and Career Counselors and Advisors
